verdicts.why: A has some good specific labels (no-self, retreat, default mode network) but many wrong members (commute post under retreat and Zen, EEG monks under Zen, a retreat diary under noble truths), generic pills (researchers, practitioners) and a 'meditation' pill holding only the research pieces. B's four pills are the reader's own categories with accurate membership and full coverage, though Meditation at 10 of 12 filters little.

B's three pills split the shelf the way this reader thinks (science, practice, philosophy) and reach every article, despite three research explainers wrongly sitting under practice and Zen missing from philosophy. A is finer-grained but its memberships are too often wrong and two labels are generic.

Both cover the whole shelf, but B's memberships are accurate and it adds a useful Retreats pill, and Buddhism plus Meditation or Neuroscience combine sensibly. A puts research explainers under practice and leaves Zen out of Buddhist philosophy; B's only weakness is a near-universal Meditation pill.
